sentences.text: After receipt of Complaint, the Complaint has been referred to the Yelahanka Police U/s 156 (3) of Cr.P.C.

Thereafter, I.O., has investigated the matter and filed chargesheet against the accused Nos.1 and 2 for the offences punishable U/s 420, 463, 120(B) of I.P.C.
 3.
Brief case of the prosecution is as under :

It is alleged in the chargesheet that, CW.1 was doing real estate business in the name of Jagruth Holding having it's office at Hunasamaranahalli village  3 C.C. No.33509/2014 situated within the jurisdiction of Yelahanka Police Station.

The accused were intended to sell property bearing Sy.99 of same village measuring 2.14 acre , as such, agreed to sell it to CW.1 for total consideration of Rs.91,50,000/- and executed an agreement on 04.11.2006 by receiving advance amount of Rs.5,00,000/-.

Further, with an intention to cheat CW.1 the accused obtained Rs.20,00,000/- again as loan, in order to repay it, accused No.1 issued two cheques on various dates to CW.1, the accused No.2 Shashidhar vs Muniraju on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117011073/
2 presented said cheques without knowledge of CW.1 and thereby, the accused have committed offences punishable u/s 420, 463, 120(B) of I.P.C.
 4.
Accused No.2 is on bail.
As the accused No.1 came to be reported as dead, case against accused No.1 is abated.
As required u/sec. 207 of Cr.PC, the copies of the charge sheet papers were furnished to the accused.
Charge was framed for the offences  4 C.C. No.33509/2014 punishable U/s 420, 463, 120(B) of I.P.C. and read over and explained to the accused in the language known to him.
Accused has pleaded not guilty and claimed for trial.

5. In order to prove the case of the prosecution,
the prosecution has examined Pws.1 and 2 and got marked Ex.P.1 and 2.
On closure of the evidence on the side of the prosecution, the statement of the accused u/sec. 313 Cr.PC came to be recorded.
The accused has denied incriminating evidence appeared against him and chose to lead defence evidence.
6. Heard the arguments.
Perused the documents placed on record.

The points that arise for consideration are :
 1. Whether the prosecution has proved  beyond all reasonable doubt that  accused has committed the offences  U/s 420, 463, 120(B) of I.P.C. ?
 5 C.C. No.33509/2014  2. What order ?
 8.

The above points are answered as under :
 Point No.1: In the Negative.

Point No.2: As per final order for the following :
 REASONS

9. Point No.1 : It is the case of the prosecution that the accused No.2 without knowledge of CW.1 presented cheques said to have been issued by CW.1 before Bank for encashment and same have been bounced and thereby the accused has committed the offenses aforesaid.
10. The prosecution in order to prove its case has examined PW.1 and 2.

PW.1 is the complainant, he stated that he had not received an advance amount of Rs.5,00,000 from accused agreeing to sell his land and CW.1 never asked him to loan of Rs.20,00,000/- and he has not issued any cheques to repay said loan and  6 C.C. No.33509/2014 same have been bounced.
He turned hostile.
PW.2 has Shashidhar vs Muniraju on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117011073/

sentences.text: 4 stated that he knows fact that accused agreed to sell land and received an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- as advance amount.

Thereafter, as per the village elders,
it was decided to sell said land to one Komala.

Further,
stated that the accused No.2 presented cheques for encasement which were issued by CW.1 in order to repay loan amount of Rs.20,00,000/- and advance amount of Rs.5,00,000/- and same have been bounced and PW.2 was not cross examined.

Admittedly, PW.1 complainant has turned hostile to the prosecution case by compromising case with accused, considering the same prayer of learned Sr.APP praying to issue summons to other witnesses was rejected.
There is no iota of evidence to prove offence alleged against accused.

11. Therefore, in view of discussion made above,
the considered opinion is of the court that, the  7 C.C. No.33509/2014 prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
The accused is entitled to benefit of doubt.
Hence, answered the point No.1 in the Negative.
